descriptionChirho: The Qal passive participle of Aramaic d-ch-l used adjectivally to describe something that inspires terror or dread, particularly of fearsome beasts and kingdoms in Daniel's visions; translations uniformly reflect the adjectival-passive sense: spa 'terrible,' arb 'هَائِلٌ/هَائِلًا' (awesome, terrifying), kor '무서운' (frightening), swa 'ya kutisha' (terrifying), hin 'भयानक/भयावह' (terrible/dreadful). Both masculine and feminine singular participle forms belong here.

The Qal active participle in the plural expressing the ongoing state or act of fearing, used of people who fear God or a king; distinct from the passive participle in that the subject experiences fear rather than causing it: spa 'y temiendo' (and fearing), arb 'وَيَخَافُونَ' (and they fear), kor '두려워하며' (fearing), swa 'na wakiogopa' (and they fearing), hin 'और डरते थे' (and they were fearing). Conjunctive-w forms are mere syntactic variants.

The Pael (intensive/causative) stem of Aramaic d-ch-l meaning to cause fear or to terrify someone, with the subject as agent of fright rather than experiencer; the causative-intensive semantics are clear across translations: eng 'it frightened me,' spa 'me atemorizó' (it terrified me), arb 'أَرْعَبَنِي' (it terrorized me), kor '나를 두렵게 했다' (made me afraid), swa 'ikanitia hofu' (it caused me fear), hin 'मुझे डरा गया' (frightened me).
